title: Get EIN
summary: Apply for an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS for the newly incorporated company.

parts.title: Pre-fill EIN application data
parts.guidance: Collect the legal name, formation details and address from the accepted entity documents. Identify the responsible party, business activity, tax classification and reason for applying. Check whether an EIN already exists and which IRS application channel the entity can use. Resolve uncertain answers with the responsible person before filing, and keep tax identifiers in the private application workspace.

parts.title: Complete IRS SS-4 form online
parts.guidance: Use the IRS application method for which the entity and responsible party qualify. Review the answers against the prepared facts and current instructions. The authorized representative approves submission; a third-party designee needs signed authorization. Complete the required identity or signature steps and save the IRS confirmation. If the applicant is ineligible for the online assistant, use the appropriate IRS alternative with accurate identity details.

verify.how: The EIN is issued in the XX-XXXXXXX format at the end of the online session — retain the CP 575 confirmation notice; banks and payroll providers ask for it.

cost.note: The IRS issues EINs for free; third-party services charge to file on your behalf.

parts.title: Store EIN in company records
parts.guidance: Save the IRS confirmation letter in the restricted company tax records. Check its legal name and EIN against the application and resolve mismatches with the filer. Use the issued letter as the source for banking and tax setup, and make it retrievable by authorized finance staff and advisers without exposing the number in public records.

metadata.supportReason: IRS EIN application is a web form with no API. System provides step-by-step guidance and pre-fills company data.

geoNotes.summary: PAN and TAN — the company's tax identifiers — are allotted automatically as part of the SPICe+ incorporation filing; the Income Tax e-filing portal is where the company then uses them.
There is no EIN application: HMRC posts the company a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) automatically after incorporation, and you register for Corporation Tax within 3 months of starting business.
The tax office issues a Steuernummer after you file the Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung (tax registration questionnaire) on ELSTER — plus a separate VAT ID from the BZSt if needed.
No application: INSEE allots the SIREN (company) and SIRET (per-establishment) identifiers automatically when the guichet unique registration lands — they arrive with the company's registration.

No separate tax-ID application: the NIPC issued at incorporation is the company's tax number (NIF), and filing the declaração de início de atividade with the tax authority activates it for corporate tax and VAT.

A CRA business number is issued automatically with federal (and most provincial) incorporation — you add program accounts to it (payroll RP, GST/HST RT, corporate tax RC) through Business Registration Online rather than applying for a separate tax ID.
